raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #56655. Include the per-block `prompt_is_token_ids` routing mask in mixed prompt-embedding prefix-cache keys, preventing a request from silently reusing KV computed for different effective inputs.

## Claims

- Changing the routing mask cannot reuse the affected prefix blocks, even when token IDs and supplied embedding tensors match.
- Identical requests still reuse cached KV. Absent/all-False masks and decode-only blocks retain existing key behavior.
- Regression coverage includes real-weight `LLM.generate` inference, block-boundary cases, both supported SHA256 hash variants, and KV event extra keys.

## Validation

Refreshed on 2026-10-29/30 after merging upstream `9a0f9b45df86b91664923ad076f27a50f69c4766` in `772751a57`:

- Full cache suites: **369 passed** in 197.63 seconds.
- Full prefix-cache E2E file: **2 passed** in 92.23 seconds, including the new real-weight cache-history regression.
- Negative control, with only the production hash helper restored to upstream behavior: **25 failed, 10 passed** among the 35 targeted cases. The new E2E test also fails at `after_a.num_cached_tokens == 0` because the observed value is **32**. No assertions were weakened between the baseline and fixed runs.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy, test-to-CI tethering, and Markdown lint. The changed documentation section also rendered locally; a hosted docs preview was not tested.

```bash
export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py -q
python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py docs/features/prompt_embeds.md
```

The cache suites require cached Hugging Face configurations or network access. Four GPUs are exposed for existing pipeline-parallel configuration tests; the E2E test itself needs one GPU. It uses the existing `hf_runner`/`vllm_runner` fixtures and Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B weights. Locally, the HF cache was populated from the same verified model revision to avoid a stalled download. The existing `v1-core` Buildkite step selects the E2E file; `v1-others-cpu` selects the CPU regressions.

The issue's A/B reproducer was also exercised in **three baseline and three fixed trials**, with token-only controls and identical inference settings:

| Observation | Unpatched main, 3/3 trials | Fixed, 3/3 trials |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B cold output | `[9, 0] * 8` | `[9, 0] * 8` |
| B after A output | `[753] * 16`, wrong | `[9, 0] * 8`, correct |
| B after A cache hit | 32 tokens, wrong reuse | 0 tokens |
| Repeated A | 32 cached tokens, correct output | 32 cached tokens, correct output |

For all three fixed trials, B's generated token IDs and first-step sampled logprobs matched its cold-cache result exactly. The new permanent E2E test uses the existing `check_logprobs_close` helper for numerical tolerance and checks both cross-mask misses and same-mask hits. JSON captures from the expanded probe retain token IDs, cached-token counts, and first-step logprobs, not a complete per-step logprob trace.

<details>
<summary>Environment and validation limits</summary>

RTX 3090, driver 580.178.04, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, Transformers 5.21.1, FP16, V2 Model Runner, FlashAttention 2, eager execution, chunked prefill, block size 16, greedy sampling, seed 0, and spawn workers. The prompt tensor repeats actual `model.embed_tokens.weight[198]` values for 33 rows. Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`; weight SHA256: `f47f71177f32bcd101b7573ec9171e6a57f4f4d31148d38e382306f42996874b`.

Python source is the merged main plus this patch. The official cu130 precompiled wheel is from ancestor `5cdbd0520e15c22e76aaf75acc1f30f42c7cd4d9`, since the exact main wheel was unavailable. The native sources, CMake/setup files, Rust sources, and requirements are identical between those revisions. This is an offline inference correctness check, not a throughput benchmark or an evaluation of other models, runners, or online serving. The hosted CI run still depends on the repository's contributor-approval gate.

</details>

## Details

`prompt_is_token_ids` selects whether each row comes from the token embedding table or the supplied tensor. Previously the hash covered the tensor but omitted this selection, so distinct effective prompts could share KV. The fix keeps the cached tensor digest and upstream's `("prompt_embeds", digest)` tag, then appends `("prompt_is_token_ids", bytes(block_mask))` when that block contains token-ID positions. This also preserves complete mask bytes in KV cache events.

The latest conflict was confined to the test helper signature. The resolution retains upstream's `sampling_params` argument together with the mixed-input arguments; production logic is unchanged from the previous revision. Added real-model regression coverage and a prefix-caching section in the existing [prompt embedding documentation](https://github.com/ai-yang/vllm/blob/fix/mixed-prompt-embeds-prefix-cache/docs/features/prompt_embeds.md#prefix-caching).

The added work is CPU mask slicing/encoding per hash block, with no new GPU synchronization or tensor transfer. Semantically equivalent inputs expressed with different masks may conservatively miss the cache; no performance improvement is claimed.

Duplicate/related work rechecked on 2026-10-29: the open `56655 in:body` search returns only this PR. The all-state `"prompt_is_token_ids" "hash"` search also finds #57076, which concerns prompt length after multimodal expansion. #51899 adds source tags but not the routing mask; #53769 concerns conformance tests; #42119 concerns differing tensor contents in external LMCache.

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, conflict resolution, regression coverage, and the validation reported above.

+### Prefix caching
+
+Prompt embeddings support [automatic prefix caching](automatic_prefix_caching.md). Enable both with `LLM(enable_prompt_embeds=True, enable_prefix_caching=True)` or `vllm serve --enable-prompt-embeds --enable-prefix-caching`.
+
+For mixed token-ID and embedding inputs, cache identity includes `prompt_is_token_ids`, which selects the source of each embedding row, as well as the token IDs and supplied embeddings. Earlier unchanged prefix blocks and repeated identical requests can still reuse cached KV.
+
 ## Online Serving
 
 Our OpenAI-compatible server accepts prompt embeddings inputs via both the [Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/completions) and the [Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat). Both are enabled by the `--enable-prompt-embeds` flag in `vllm serve`.
